security.notes: Every Phase 3b handler in src/main/ipc/claude.ts calls assertRendererFrame(event) before any service work, then .parse() input via Zod, then .parse() output before return. The handler-entry .parse() is exhaustively tested at the unit layer (every reject row asserts the service was NOT called, e.g. `expect(claudeService.repoState).not.toHaveBeenCalled()` after a missing/empty slug). The ClaudeService never executes user-controlled strings directly — `launch` only constructs a `claude` CLI command line via buildLaunchCommand (pinned by 7 unit tests) and shellSingleQuote (pinned by 5 unit tests) and delegates to launcherService.openInTerminal — never spawns a subprocess itself. The openClaudeMd path resolves an editor URL via buildEditorFileUrl (pinned by __claude_build_editor_file_url tests) and goes through openExternalAllowlisted from @main/security/allowlist (NOT direct shell.openExternal). Filesystem reads via fs.readFileSync / fs.createReadStream / fs.statSync; the JSONL parser is defensive (silently skips malformed lines, doesn't trust the wire format). The chokidar watcher subscribes only to `~/.claude/projects/` and ignores any non-.jsonl event, validated by tests/unit/main/claude/watcher.spec.ts. Not a 5 because (a) the encodeURI() gap from Phase 3a is still present in src/main/services/claude.ts buildEditorFileUrl (carried over — same encodeURI behaviour for vscode/cursor/zed/windsurf file:// schemes; JetBrains/Sublime correctly encodeURIComponent), and (b) the production Electron build is still not automated-tested for non-allowlisted file:// URL rejection (carried over from earlier phases).

observability.notes: Test-failure observability is strong: every Zod-reject row in the new IPC handler spec asserts `expect(serviceMethod).not.toHaveBeenCalled()` as a second guard so a regression that silently swallows the Zod error is caught. The watcher spec uses fake timers + a captured handler array so a debounce regression prints exactly which event/hash collapsed where. The transcript parser uses temp JSONL files with deterministic timestamps, so a startedAt/lastActivityAt regression prints the exact ISO string. The E2E spec carries a verbose console.warn when the catalog is empty and the test falls through to the /claude global-usage assertion — easier to diagnose than a silent skip.

issues.description: Carried over from Phase 3a: Playwright Electron global setup (tests/e2e/_global-setup.ts) unconditionally calls `pnpm electron:rebuild`, which invokes `pnpm exec electron-rebuild -f -w better-sqlite3 -w find-git-repositories`. On Node 21.2.0 (the developer's current host) this fails with `SyntaxError: The requested module 'node:util' does not provide an export named 'styleText'` — `styleText` lands in Node 22.x. The project's engines field already says `>=20.19.0 <21 || >=22` so the dev environment is technically out of spec, but the rebuild script has a documented fallback (`electron-builder install-app-deps`) that works fine on Node 21 (manually verified during Phase 3a + Phase 3b QE). Fix: either (a) extend scripts/rebuild-natives.mjs to try `electron-rebuild` and fall through to `electron-builder install-app-deps` on a SyntaxError/ESM-import-resolve failure, or (b) pin CI + dev docs to Node 22+. Blocks the Phase 3a E2E specs (process-flow.spec.ts + launcher-flow.spec.ts) AND the Phase 3b E2E spec (claude-flow.spec.ts) from running in this environment. Reproduction: `pnpm exec playwright test --config playwright.electron.config.ts` from the project root on a Node 21.x host.

Carried over from Phase 3a + extended: src/main/services/launcher.ts `buildEditorUrl` AND src/main/services/claude.ts `buildEditorFileUrl` both use `encodeURI()` for the file:// scheme variants (vscode, cursor, zed, windsurf) — encodeURI does NOT escape `?` or `#`. A repo / CLAUDE.md path containing either character could in theory leak the rest of the path into the URL's query or fragment when shell.openExternal opens the resulting URL. macOS paths almost never contain `?` or `#` so this is LOW severity. The JetBrains and Sublime builders use `encodeURIComponent()` and correctly escape both characters — pinned by tests/unit/main/services/launcher.spec.ts AND tests/unit/main/services/claude.spec.ts (the `__claude_build_editor_file_url` test 'encodes ? and # in the file param for JetBrains/Sublime'). Current behaviour is pinned so a future fix can't regress silently.

tests/e2e/claude-flow.spec.ts has a documented fallback branch: when the catalog DB is empty in the test environment (no seeded repos), it skips the repo-detail-tab path and asserts the /claude global-usage route instead. Reasoning: this build's catalog DB is populated by a real filesystem scan + Ollama embedding — out of scope for an automated suite. The Claude tab itself is exercised at the unit layer (240 unit tests across 7 spec files cover every test seam in ClaudeService + the registry / transcript / repo-claude / watcher / usage modules + every IPC handler). If a future test environment seeds the catalog with a fixture repo containing a `.claude/` directory, the fallback branch should be removed and a dedicated assertion of the four section headings (Skills/Agents/MCP/Sessions) should run unconditionally.

Carried over from Phase 3a: tests/e2e/process-flow.spec.ts second test ('spawned http server surfaces in /processes table') accepts the empty state as a pass when the main-side lsof poller doesn't surface the spawned child within 15 seconds. The E2E spec is best-effort detection coverage; if a future test environment can reliably surface a Node-spawned http listener via lsof, the warn-and-skip branch should be removed.
